requirement:
When replacing results for an unfiltered workspace invocation or a filtered
invocation selecting at least one test, a prepared build configuration
incompatible with the active configuration under
{cite}`requirements.test-coverage.storage.configuration` clears the whole
current set and becomes active in the same atomic replacement, before test
execution.

Results from the previous configuration do not reappear when that
configuration is selected again. A filtered invocation selecting no tests
leaves the current results and active configuration unchanged under
{cite}`requirements.test-coverage.storage.replace`.
rationale:
**Obligations derived from `requirements.test-coverage.storage.configuration_reset`**
1. An unfiltered invocation, or a filtered invocation selecting at least one test, with an incompatible build configuration clears the whole current set. The new configuration becomes active in the same atomic replacement, before any test runs.
2. Results from the old configuration do not come back when that configuration is selected again.
3. A filtered invocation selecting no tests leaves the current results and active configuration unchanged.

**Coverage**
- **Filtered, at least one test, incompatible.** `src/execution_coverage/store.rs#mod[tests]/fn[incompatible_builds_reset_every_test_but_empty_focused_runs_do_not]` first builds config `a` with two tests, one of them completed. It then replaces with a filtered one-test run under config `b`. It asserts the active configuration is `b`, only one test remains, and that test has no measurements. Both the clearing of the unselected `b` test and the configuration switch are checked.
- **No reappearance.** The same test switches back to `a` with a filtered run selecting only test `b`. It asserts exactly one test remains, `b`, with no measurements. The earlier `a` results do not return.
- **Unfiltered, incompatible.** The same test completes two tests under `a` with value 7, then runs an unfiltered replace under `b` selecting one test. It asserts config `b`, a single test, `a` pending, and no measurements. The earlier results are cleared and the selected test is reset to pending.
- **Filtered, no tests selected.** The same test calls `replace` with an empty filtered selection under config `b`. It asserts the call returns `false`, then records the empty invocation. The snapshot keeps config `a`, both tests and the existing measurements. Only the latest invocation changes, and that is allowed.
- **Atomic, same replacement.** `failed_atomic_replacement_preserves_results_configuration_and_invocation` in the same file injects a write failure into an incompatible replacement from `a` to `b`. It asserts that the error is returned and that the configuration, the latest invocation, and the result with its measurements all stay as before. This shows the clearing and the activation of the new configuration are committed together or not at all.
- **Before execution.** `tests/execution_coverage.rs#fn[a_failed_replacement_commit_reports_the_error_without_launching_execution]` runs an incompatible CLI invocation (`--features alpha` after a default-feature run) with a commit failure injected. It asserts that the command fails with the error, that no nextest execution is launched (a sentinel file is never created), and that the runs, measurements and profiles are unchanged. The store test shows that `replace` alone leaves the new configuration active with pending entries before any completion is recorded.

Each of these tests carries a {test} reference to the subject. The determination of what counts as incompatible is delegated to `requirements.test-coverage.storage.configuration`, which is cited context, and the general replacement semantics are covered under `requirements.test-coverage.storage.replace`. I found no unmet obligation or marking gap.

text: :::{req} storage.configuration_reset
When replacing results for an unfiltered workspace invocation or a filtered
invocation selecting at least one test, a prepared build configuration
incompatible with the active configuration under
{cite}`requirements.test-coverage.storage.configuration` clears the whole
current set and becomes active in the same atomic replacement, before test
execution.
Results from the previous configuration do not reappear when that
configuration is selected again. A filtered invocation selecting no tests
leaves the current results and active configuration unchanged under
{cite}`requirements.test-coverage.storage.replace`.
:::{req} storage.configuration
Each coverage record MUST identify the recorded toolchain, compilation target,
Cargo build profile, enabled features, and instrumentation-affecting compiler
settings. These settings MUST determine build-configuration compatibility for
the combined view. A nextest scheduling profile alone MUST NOT make otherwise
compatible build configurations incompatible.
:::{req} storage.replace
After preparation and selection discovery succeed, and before any selected
test starts, Habeas atomically establishes the new coverage set:
- An unfiltered workspace invocation clears the entire previous set,
including results for tests that no longer exist. This includes
`habeas coverage` with no supplied arguments and `habeas test`.
- An invocation with an explicit package or binary restriction, test filter,
partition, or ignored-only selection is filtered. It clears results for all
selected test identities and preserves unselected results within the
active build configuration.
- Every selected test receives a pending entry without measurements.
Native default filters and the default handling of ignored tests still apply
to an unfiltered workspace invocation. `--run-ignored all` alone does not make
a workspace invocation filtered.
A selected test that never starts because of fail-fast, interruption, or
execution startup failure remains unavailable. Its previous result does not
become available again. A filtered selection containing no tests leaves the
current results and active configuration unchanged; an empty unfiltered
workspace selection clears the previous set.
If the atomic replacement cannot be committed, the command reports the
failure and starts no tests. The previously committed coverage set and active
configuration remain unchanged.
